newsitem.title: USA: CANADIAN SPOT NATGAS SOFTENS ON FUTURES, WEATHER.
newsitem.headline: CANADIAN SPOT NATGAS SOFTENS ON FUTURES, WEATHER.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices drifted lower Friday as futures reversed their trend and cooler temperatures arrived in Alberta, market sources said.

Spot prices at the AECO storage hub in Alberta fell an average of three cents to C$1.48-1.49 per gigajoule. September AECO was also talked down two cents to C$1.42, while one-year business was offered at C$1.73.
Temperatures in Calgary were forecast to reach highs around 70 degrees F over the weekend, according to Weather Services Corp.

Petro-Canada's Hanlan-Robb gas plant west of Edmonton in Alberta is expected to return to half power by Saturday and full power by Monday afternoon. The unit was taken off line Wednesday for a scheduled turnaround, affecting about 200 million cubic feet per day of gas.
At Sumas, Wash., spot gas prices also lost about three cents to about $1.10 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
In the East, Niagara prices slipped 11 cents to $2.50-2.51 as NYMEX's September contract retreated to a low of $2.375.

Separately, Canadian Gas Association said overall gas stocks were at 277.56 bcf, or 56.1 percent full. This compared with 58.1 percent full a year ago. In the West, stocks were at 157.26 bcf, or 60 percent full, versus 63.7 percent a year ago. Eastern stocks were at 120.3 bcf, or 51.7 percent full, just slightly higher than a year ago.
